copy.blurb:
Belgium face Egypt on Monday, evening UTC kickoff, in FIFA World Cup 2026. This is one of the matches where the model's number disagrees with the closing line on Polymarket — a substantive gap on the Egypt side, +9.4pp.

Elo numbers going in: Belgium 1860, Egypt 1760. That's a 100-point lead for Belgium — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Belgium to win at 49%, the draw at 24%, and Egypt to win at 27%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Belgium to win at 58%, the draw at 24%, and Egypt to win at 18%. The Egypt side trades at 18% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +456. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 27%, +9.4pp wider.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Egypt, that haircut lands the model at 22%; the market is at 18%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +4.4pp. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Egypt side.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff 25 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Egypt a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +9.4pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.

editorial_citations.quote: Liverpool forward Mohamed Salah is named in Egypt's preliminary World Cup squad, which will be trimmed by one player this month.

copy.summary: On Egypt, the model is +9.4pp out from Polymarket. Our number reads 27%; the market reads 18%. That gap is the basis for the Pick.
copy.title: Belgium v Egypt · the model leans Egypt
